statement: P2P SSD→GPU DMA is slower than bounce (DRAM intermediary) when NVMe and GPU are on different root complexes at SYS level (cross-NUMA, crossing AMD Infinity Fabric). The penalty is ~65% at SYS level regardless of iteration.
regime: AMD EPYC multi-socket systems where NVMe NUMA node != GPU NUMA node (SYS-level PCIe topology)
mechanism: SYS-level P2P DMA from NVMe (NUMA 1, root complex 0000:c0) to GPU BAR1 (NUMA 0, root complex 0000:40) traverses the AMD Infinity Fabric inter-socket link. Each 128 KiB chunk adds ~100-200ns per cache line for the cross-NUMA routing, adding 6-12ms total for 32 chunks. The bounce path avoids this by using DRAM on the CPU side, then cudaMemcpy (which uses the GPU's own DMA engine for the DRAM→GPU leg).
applicability_bounds: Applies to sequential (QD=1) read workloads. At high QD with P2P+BatchSubmit this penalty may be overcome by parallelism. Specific to AMD EPYC Milan topology; Intel Xeon may differ.

statement: P2P SSD→GPU DMA with NODE-level PCIe topology (same NUMA node, different root complexes within same CPU socket) is faster than the bounce path, not merely less penalized. The advantage is ~2x (0.49 ratio) for 4 MiB objects at sequential QD=1.
regime: AMD EPYC single-socket path: NVMe and GPU both on NUMA 0 but on different root complexes (0000:60 vs 0000:40), sequential QD=1, 4 MiB objects, 128 KiB chunks
mechanism: At NODE level, DMA from NVMe (63:00.0, root complex 0000:60) to GPU BAR1 (root complex 0000:40) stays within one CPU socket — no Infinity Fabric traversal. The intra-socket PCIe fabric provides lower per-hop latency. The P2P path also eliminates the bounce buffer write (DRAM) and cudaMemcpy steps. These two savings together make P2P faster than bounce at NODE level despite the cross-root-complex penalty remaining.
applicability_bounds: Requires NODE-level or closer topology (NVMe and GPU on same NUMA node). Confounded by device heterogeneity (63:00.0 vs c2:00.0 have different raw NVMe speeds). Medium confidence because we cannot compare P2P and bounce on the same NVMe device for both NODE and SYS conditions.

statement: The PCIe topology effect (NODE vs SYS) on P2P performance is dominated by the AMD Infinity Fabric traversal, not the number of root complex hops per se. NODE-level topology eliminates the inter-socket link and transforms P2P from a 65% penalty to a 2x advantage.
regime: AMD EPYC Milan dual-socket systems with NVMe and GPU on different root complexes but same NUMA node (NODE-level) vs different NUMA nodes (SYS-level)
mechanism: At SYS level: NVMe (NUMA 1) → Infinity Fabric → GPU (NUMA 0) adds the inter-socket link latency (~400 GB/s shared bandwidth, ~200ns/cache line). At NODE level: NVMe (NUMA 0) → intra-socket PCIe fabric → GPU (NUMA 0) bypasses Infinity Fabric entirely. The P2P ratio change from 1.643 (SYS) to 0.491 (NODE) is a 3.3x improvement, attributable to eliminating the Infinity Fabric traversal for 32 × 128 KiB sequential DMA operations.
applicability_bounds: Specific to AMD EPYC Milan architecture. Effect applies to sequential P2P; may be different for batched/parallel P2P. Confidence is medium because device heterogeneity (63:00.0 vs c2:00.0) prevents clean isolation.

statement: Multi-iteration SSD-tier benchmarks that compare paths with different memory-tier promotion policies produce invalid comparisons: the bounce path's lower multi-iteration average reflects DRAM caching (not faster SSD transfer), while the P2P no-promotion path's higher multi-iteration average reflects repeated cold SSD reads (by design).
regime: Any certus-server benchmark comparing bounce (with memory-tier promotion) vs P2P (without promotion) using --bench-iterations > 1
mechanism: The bounce path calls dm.create_memory_tier_entry() after each SSD read, so subsequent iterations hit memory-tier instead of SSD. The P2P path (in our implementation) does NOT update the dispatch map (leaves as BlockDevice), so every iteration re-reads from SSD. After iteration 1, bounce measures DRAM latency while P2P measures SSD latency — they're no longer comparable.
applicability_bounds: Always applies to bench-iterations > 1 when comparing bounce (promotes) vs P2P (no-promote). Use --bench-iterations 1 for valid first-hit comparison.

statement: Caching prepare_memory_for_spdk results (keyed by 64-byte CUDA IPC handle) successfully eliminates per-lookup P2P overhead. The DmaBuffer cache works correctly: prepare_memory_for_spdk is called once per unique handle and subsequent lookups reuse the cached registration. However, eliminating this overhead does not make P2P competitive when PCIe topology causes P2P DMA to be inherently slower than bounce.
regime: Dispatcher v1 with gpu_dma_cache Mutex<HashMap<[u8;64], Arc<Mutex<DmaBuffer>>>>
mechanism: The benchmark pre-allocates one lookup tensor; all 10 objects share the same 64-byte IPC handle. The cache is populated on the first lookup and reused for all subsequent ones. This is confirmed by the consistency of per-object latency (single cache entry, stable behavior).
applicability_bounds: Applies when benchmark uses a single reusable GPU buffer (test_client.py line 344). In a multi-handle workload, cache size would grow linearly with unique handles.

statement: Before implementing P2P, verify PCIe topology — NVMe and GPU must be at least NODE-level (same NUMA) for P2P to be viable. Cross-root-complex at SYS level adds 65% latency penalty. Cross-root-complex at NODE level enables P2P advantage (~2x speedup). Same-root-complex (best case) has not been tested on this hardware.
regime: AMD EPYC Milan dual-socket, SPDK P2P via GDRCopy/IGpuServices::prepare_memory_for_spdk
mechanism: See RP-9, RP-10. SYS-level penalty attributed to Infinity Fabric; NODE-level advantage attributed to elimination of Infinity Fabric with intra-socket routing. No same-root-complex NVMe+GPU combination exists on this hardware.
applicability_bounds: Specific to this test system (AMD EPYC Milan, 8 root complexes, no NVMe on same root complex as any GPU). Must re-verify on different systems.
